A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 25-page versions of the same OrbEvo paper. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–N support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDDFT simulations and OrbEvo evaluations on QM9 and malonaldehyde, including quantitative results, predicted trajectories, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and model-evaluation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The architectures, electronic-state interactions, conditioning, time bundling, and push-forward training are unchanged. Both versions already specify delta-wavefunction prediction in Equation 4; explicitly using delta coefficients in Equation 10 resolves the loss description rather than establishing a new training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5,000 QM9 molecules and 1,500 malonaldehyde configurations, with unchanged wavefunction, dipole, absorption, larger-molecule generalization, and global-phase evaluations.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods and ablation variants are unchanged. Table 12 renames Pool-sall-noise to WF-sall-noise, matching the existing wavefunction-pooling model; its scores and comparison membership remain identical.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes the reported delta-rescaling parameter beta from 1,000 to 1 × 10^-3. This corrects a stated preprocessing setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. Splits, simulation settings, training budgets, and evaluation designs otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The appendices retain the same sampling, conditioning, density-matrix, training-strategy, equivariance, distribution-shift, time-bundling, global-phase, and noise-injection analyses. No analysis or supporting evidence is added or removed.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including Table 6's simulation timing averaged over 40 simulations. No repeated-seed reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Numerical results, timings, rankings, and plotted findings are retained throughout. For example, Table 2 reports the same QM9 DM-s8 rollout nRMSE of 0.1885 and absorption nRMSE of 0.0752. Table 12 changes only a model label.

T1.justification: Correcting beta to 10^-3 makes Equation 3's 1/beta factor consistent with the stated amplification of delta coefficients. This is a local mathematical consistency correction; the TDDFT derivations, symmetry assumptions, and appendix mathematics otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about equivariant wavefunction evolution, electronic-state interactions, physical-property prediction, and molecular generalization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of density-matrix interactions, sampling, rollout stability, and larger-molecule generalization are unchanged. The limitations concerning conical intersections and exchange-correlation functionals are also retained.

D1.justification: The corrected beta value and explicit identification of delta coefficients as the loss inputs clarify reproduction of the preprocessing and training specification. Hardware, software, Table 13 hyperparameters, dataset-generation details, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references and Appendix A retain the same cited works, comparisons with prior approaches, and positioning of direct time-dependent wavefunction learning.

P1.justification: Localized edits correct feature-index notation, clarify Equation 10 and its reference to Equation 3, and standardize the WF model name in Table 12. There is no broader rewriting or section reorganization.

P2.justification: Table 12's model-row label is corrected, and the notation edits cause limited equation and paragraph reflow. Figures, table structures, captions, and their placement are otherwise unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes the reciprocal-scaling inconsistency around Equation 3, aligns Equation 10 with the already-described delta prediction target, and removes an inconsistent model label in Table 12. These corrections improve technical clarity and reproducibility, while the empirical evidence, scientific scope, and limitations remain unchanged.
